lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - A Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops reading skills through a text about paint colours. Students read to understand the concepts of primary and secondary colours and learn new related vocabulary.
Look for students actively following the text as they listen and showing comprehension of the colour-mixing process described.
“We've learned about art class, but how do artists make so many colours? Let's read this story about Jenny to discover the secret of primary and secondary colours.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - B. Choose the correct answers

details: Choose the correct answers assesses comprehension of the reading passage. Students demonstrate their understanding of the text’s main idea and the art concepts by selecting the correct answers.
Look for accurate selection of the answers for all three questions, showing that students have understood the key information from the text.
“That was a very colourful story! Now let's see what we've learned about painting. Read the questions and choose the correct answers to show you're a colour expert!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.113-115 - A Listen and point

details: Listen and point introduces the concept of soft c and soft g sounds. Students listen to the words and point to the pictures, connecting the spoken sound to the visual.
Look for focused listening and accurate pointing to the corresponding pictures for each word.

“Do you know what letter starts the colour cyan or what letter makes the ‘j’ sound in ‘orange’? Sometimes the letters 'c' and 'g' don't make their usual sound. Let's listen carefully to hear their secret soft sounds.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.113-115 - B Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle reinforces the different spelling patterns for the soft c and soft g sounds. Students listen for the word and circle the correct grapheme.
Look for careful listening and correct circling of the grapheme that matches the word they hear.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.113-115 - A Read and match

details: Read and match strengthens word recognition for soft c and soft g words. Students read the target vocabulary and draw lines to connect each word to the correct image.
Look for accurate reading of the target words and correctly drawn lines connecting the words to the pictures.
“Can you read the words with our new soft 'c' and 'g' sounds, and help me match them to the right pictures?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.113-115 - C Draw a blue line under the soft c and an orange line under the soft g words

details: Draw a... line... reinforces grapheme recognition. Students scan the text to locate words with the target sounds and underline them in the correct colour to show they can differentiate them.
Look for accurate identification of all target words and correct use of the colours for the soft c and soft g spelling patterns.
